title: Seeing the Dorsey Brothers at Skateland and choosing drums
summary: Seeing the Dorsey Brothers with Louie Bellson and Charlie Shavers in July 1956 leads him to ask for drums and buy Ellington Uptown.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well he wanted me to be exposed to music. I’m not sure he wanted it to go quite the way it went, as you will find out later in the interview. But I walked into that thing, it was July of 1956. And at that time Jackie Gleason was big, but he would have a summer replacement and it was Tommy and Jimmy Dorsey. In fact, that summer replacement — one of the episodes of the summer replacement was when the juggler was on the show of the Dorsey Brothers, when Charlie Parker was watching it, as he died. In fact in the movie you see the juggler and in the scene when he’s in the Stanhope Hotel with the Baroness de Koenigswarter, they used the actual scene. Well that summer they also went on the road. So anyway I walked in there, and the drummer was Louis Bellson. He was married to Pearl Bailey. And she was in an automobile sitting behind the place, she didn’t come in. But he drove separately from the band. And he did a drum solo — now I’m not a hundred percent sure it was “Skin Deep,” because that was what he did with Duke Ellington. But, since it was his arrangement and I’m sure he owned the rights to it, it very well could have been “Skin Deep.” I just know that it was pretty deep. And I watched it. And Charlie Shavers was playing trumpet, Lee Castle was in the trumpet section, which is neither here nor there, Frank Maynes, and then they broke down to the — I think they call it the Clambake Seven when they went to a Dixieland band. But the band was ferocious man, absolutely ferocious. And Louie Bellson was ferocious. So I said to my father, I said, “why don’t I try the drums?” So we went down to a local music store. And he wasn’t going to buy me a set of drums, because he had seen me lose interest in the other things. So we bought a practice pad, a pair of drum sticks, and Duke Ellington’s “Ellington Uptown,” which featured Louis Bellson playing “Skin Deep.” Well from then on it was pretty much drums for me.
Louie Bellson was with the Dorsey Brothers after Ellington?
Yes. That record, that “Ellington Uptown” I believe was in ’52 or ‘3, and they came here in ’56. It was July of ’56. For Christmas that year — I had never touched the drums up
